In an in-depth interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop application and discussed plans for a future tabless interface. The full interview can be viewed below.

In the future, users will be able to get work done seamlessly within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern debuted a preview clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand-new YouTube channel, New Things.

Stern published the full interview today, covering the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware development plans, its lawsuit with Apple, and the earlier data leak on Hugging Face.

During the interview, Stern noted that OpenAI had previously decided to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop applications and launch a new agent mode called Work.

The merged interface caused considerable confusion, particularly for users who simply wanted to continue using ChatGPT but had trouble locating their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the application, adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top of the interface and introducing a dropdown menu in the sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. Although it is no longer as difficult as before, the interface remains somewhat complex.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a bit confusing," adding that it was a "transitional arrangement" toward the future, and that eventually the Work tab would disappear, with its functionality "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also stated that, despite the confusing rollout of the merged application, OpenAI had achieved its expected results, with Codex's user base soaring from 5 million to 10 million within just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was purely the result of forcibly bundling Codex into the ChatGPT application, Brockman again conceded the point, but argued that, to a certain extent, it was also part of the plan:

The entire interview is excellent and absolutely worth watching. It also features a very Joanna Stern-style segment where she attempts to bring ChatGPT Voice into the conversation—and the results are exactly what you would expect.
